_comment: TENNESSEE FORECLOSURE NOTICES. Free, statewide, and mandated by law.
Tennessee changed its foreclosure notice law effective July 2025. Every
foreclosure notice published in any Tennessee newspaper must now also be
posted to a free public statewide repository. The Tennessee Press Association
runs foreclosurestn.com as that central repository. Notices are also posted by
third party posting companies under TCA 35-5-101, and all Tennessee public
notices appear at tnpublicnotice.com.
This matters because Tennessee foreclosures are non judicial. There is no
court docket to scrape, which normally makes pre foreclosure the hardest free
signal to get in this state. The statewide repository closes that gap for all
eight of your target counties at zero cost.
SET THE URL FIRST. The page structure was not verifiable when this was written,
so the urls are placeholders rather than guesses. Open the site, find the page
that actually lists notices for your county, and paste its url. Then:
gf discover tn-foreclosure-statewide
If the table is not found, the error lists every table on the page with its
headers, so setting requireHeaders is a copy and paste. If it reports no
tables at all, the page is rendered by JavaScript and you will need the site's
own export or search-by-county url instead.
Prefer requireHeaders over tableIndex. A site redesign moves indexes around but
rarely renames columns.

sources.label: Tennessee statewide foreclosure notice repository
notes: Start at foreclosurestn.com, the Tennessee Press Association repository.
A substitute trustee sale notice carries a scheduled sale date, so the event
is recorded as a foreclosure rather than a pre foreclosure. The field mapper
should pick up a Sale Date column as the auction date and a Trustee column
as the lender. Confirm both with gf discover.
An auction inside 60 days adds to the distress score and flips the strategy
to subject_to or cash, since a seller on a deadline needs cash, not terms.
minIntervalMs is 1000 here. This is a press association site, not a county

sources.name: tn-tax-delinquent-example
sources.label: County trustee delinquent tax list, example shape
notes: Most Tennessee county trustees publish a delinquent tax list, usually once a
year and often as an HTML table or a PDF. If it is a CSV, use kind csv
instead. If it is a PDF, there is no connector for that: copy it into a
spreadsheet, save as CSV, and point the csv connector at a local file url.
Tax delinquency plus high equity is one of the strongest seller finance
combinations, because the owner has a bill and no loan to pay off.
